answer: Special Ops mask rule: graders never learn whose quill wrote what. Before any seat opens, the network runs every answer through a neutral rewriter that keeps the idea but scrubs wording, punctuation habits and any hidden watermark, then shuffles it into the epoch's pile. A farm's thousand keys can't spot their siblings to rubber-stamp, since every planted signal is washed out by dawn: their easy 3s scatter onto strangers and their own fakes get graded cold.
